M0118-0008 (2026-06-22): create-trigger promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationCreateTrigger (design 0118-0027) — CREATE TRIGGER now takes a transaction-scoped ShareRowExclusiveLock on the table via acquireDDLLockTxn while INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE take a transaction-scoped RowExclusiveLock via acquireWriteLockTxn (write/DDL siblings of the existing scan-read AccessShare acquireScanReadLockTxn) so a concurrent UPDATE blocks until the CREATE TRIGGER transaction commits while a concurrent SELECT FOR UPDATE proceeds — byte-identical to PG 18.3; the rest of the M0118-0008 DDL/VACUUM group stays deferred (alter-table-* need ADD/VALIDATE CONSTRAINT lock semantics; the *-conflict family — truncate-conflict vacuum-conflict cluster-conflict — needs CREATE ROLE/GRANT/SET ROLE privilege infrastructure; reindex-schema needs REINDEX SCHEMA CONCURRENTLY parsing; multiple-cic needs CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY waiting; inherit-temp needs cross-backend temp-relation inheritance exclusion). M0118-0008 (2026-06-22): sequence-ddl promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationSequenceDdl (design 0118-0028) — nextval() now takes a transaction-scoped RowExclusiveLock on the sequence relation (new acquireSequenceLockTxn: held to commit inside an explicit transaction; transient acquire+release under the per-statement backend identity in autocommit so the wait still happens during acquisition) and ALTER SEQUENCE takes an AccessExclusiveLock via acquireDDLLockTxn; the two conflict per the standard lock matrix so a concurrent nextval blocks while another session is mid-ALTER SEQUENCE and a later ALTER SEQUENCE waits for an in-progress nextval to commit — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all five permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-22): reindex-concurrently promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationReindexConcurrently (design 0118-0029) — REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY now parses CONCURRENTLY in the modern post-type position (REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY name) and waits for every transaction holding a lock on the table to finish via the WaitForLockers analog (*Context).waitForRelationLockers (polls tableLockMgr.Holders and returns once no other backend holds a lock; it takes no lock of its own so concurrent reads in AccessShare and writes in RowExclusive proceed unimpeded — the CONCURRENTLY contract since REINDEX holds only ShareUpdateExclusive) so a REINDEX issued while another session has the table open reports waiting and completes only after that transaction commits while a REINDEX started before any concurrent table access returns immediately — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all six permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-22): reindex-schema promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationReindexSchema (design 0118-0030) — REINDEX SCHEMA now locks every non-virtual user table in the schema in OID (creation) order; a plain reindex takes a ShareLock per relation (which conflicts with a concurrent SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE holder so it waits) while REINDEX SCHEMA CONCURRENTLY waits for lockers without taking a conflicting lock; the OID-ordered stall lands on the earliest-created locked table first so a concurrent DROP of a later not-yet-reached table proceeds while the reindex waits — both permutations byte-identical to PG 18.3 via the new (*Context).acquireRelLockMaybeTransient helper (held-to-commit in an explicit transaction or transient acquire+release in autocommit). M0118-0008 (2026-06-22): multiple-cic promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationMultipleCic (design 0118-0031) — a partial-index WHERE predicate referencing no table columns is now const-folded (evaluated exactly once at build time via the new exported planner.ExprContainsColumnRef guard + evalExpr mirroring PG eval_const_expressions in BuildIndexInfo) so two simultaneous CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY builds whose IMMUTABLE advisory-lock predicates run on empty tables block correctly; CreateIndexStmt.Concurrently is now recorded by the parser and a concurrent build captures the active-transaction slots at its start (mvcc SnapshotActiveOtherSlots refactored out of WaitForOlderSlotsToCommit) and drains them after the build (WaitForSlotsToCommit) so the newer build completes only after the older one — snapshotting at start not at wait time avoids a mutual wait between two simultaneous builds — and the runner (*) star branch now drains ungated pending steps before the star step's own completion (partitionGatedOn keeps BlockerStepComplete-gated steps such as deadlock-hard s7a8 reported after) matching isolationtester dispatch-order completion; byte-identical to PG 18.3. M0118-0008 (2026-06-22): alter-table-3 promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationAlterTable3 (design 0118-0032) — ALTER TABLE ENABLE/DISABLE TRIGGER now takes a transaction-scoped ShareRowExclusiveLock via acquireDDLLockTxn (mirrors PG AlterTableGetLockLevel) so a concurrent INSERT in RowExclusiveLock blocks until the ALTER transaction commits while a concurrent SELECT FOR UPDATE in RowShareLock proceeds; additionally when a statement errors at the top level of a transaction (no open savepoint) the aborted transaction's heavyweight table locks are now released immediately in connTxState.Fail() mirroring PG AbortTransaction releasing locks at abort rather than at the explicit ROLLBACK so a later conflicting ALTER in another session does not wait on the aborted transaction; byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all 48 permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-22): vacuum-skip-locked promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationVacuumSkipLocked (design 0118-0033) — VACUUM/ANALYZE (SKIP_LOCKED) now take a conditional per-relation lock (the new (*Context).tryAcquireMaintenanceLock mirroring ConditionalLockRelationOid: ShareUpdateExclusiveLock or AccessExclusiveLock for VACUUM FULL) and skip a contended relation; a relation the user named explicitly emits a WARNING skipping vacuum/analyze of X --- lock not available while a partition reached by expanding a partitioned table is skipped silently; ANALYZE of a partitioned parent then reads every leaf partition under a blocking AccessShareLock for inheritance statistics (analyzeInheritanceWait via acquireRelLockMaybeTransient) so it waits on a child held in ACCESS EXCLUSIVE but not SHARE; the isolation runner now echoes each server message with its real protocol severity (WARNING vs NOTICE from pq.Error.Severity) instead of a hard-coded NOTICE; byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all sixteen permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-22): vacuum-concurrent-drop promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationVacuumConcurrentDrop (design 0118-0035) — without SKIP_LOCKED VACUUM/ANALYZE now take a blocking per-relation ShareUpdateExclusiveLock via acquireRelLockMaybeTransient (mirrors vacuum.c vacuum_open_relation → LockRelationOid) so they wait behind a concurrent LOCK ... IN SHARE MODE rather than proceeding immediately; after the lock is taken a target relation that a concurrently committing transaction DROPped is re-detected via the new relationStillExists helper (LookupTableByOID mirroring PG try_relation_open) and skipped — emitting a WARNING skipping vacuum/analyze of X --- relation no longer exists only for an explicitly named relation while a partition child reached by expanding a partitioned table is skipped silently; byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all six permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-22): inherit-temp promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationInheritTemp (design 0118-0037) — inheritance expansion of a persistent parent now excludes another session's temporary children (RELATION_IS_OTHER_TEMP) via catalog.AccessibleInheritanceChildren wired at the planner SELECT site (session token threaded through SearchPathCatalog.TempOwnerToken/CurrentTempOwner + planner.currentTempOwner) and the executor UPDATE/DELETE/UPDATE-FROM/DELETE-USING/TRUNCATE expansion sites (owner from sessionTempOwner(ctx)); the cross-session plan cache is bypassed when catalog.HasTempInheritanceChildren() is true so one session's inh_parent plan is never served to another; TRUNCATE now takes a transaction-scoped AccessExclusiveLock and a bare autocommit scan takes a transient AccessShareLock so s2_select_p blocks behind s1's in-progress TRUNCATE inh_parent while s2_select_c on its own temp child proceeds — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all nine permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-23): truncate-conflict promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationTruncateConflict (design 0118-0039) — TRUNCATE now enforces table privileges so SET ROLE to a role lacking the grant fails immediately with permission denied for table truncate_tab (42501) without waiting while after GRANT TRUNCATE the command succeeds and instead blocks behind a concurrent session holding the table open; added a catalog ACL store (Catalog.GrantTablePrivilege/HasTablePrivilege/DropTableACL) plus SET ROLE/RESET ROLE effective-role tracking plus an autocommit table-level GRANT recorder plus a pre-lock privilege check in execTruncate (acquireRelLockMaybeTransient so a granted autocommit TRUNCATE still waits for a conflicting lock) plus a fix for the CREATE-ROLE batch-swallow that previously dropped the trailing CREATE TABLE in the spec one-batch setup; byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all eight permutations M0118-0008 (2026-06-23): vacuum-conflict and cluster-conflict promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationVacuumConflict and TestPort_IsolationClusterConflict (design 0118-0040) — VACUUM/ANALYZE now run the maintenance-privilege check vacuum_is_permitted_to_vacuum BEFORE taking any lock: a non-superuser SET ROLE session that does not own the relation skips it immediately with a permission denied to vacuum/analyze X skipping it WARNING (no wait) emitted in expand_vacuum_rel/expandAnalyzeTargets from the pg_class data with no lock; after ALTER TABLE ... OWNER TO records the owning role on catalog.Table.Owner the role owns the table so VACUUM/ANALYZE are permitted and block on a conflicting LOCK ... IN SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE MODE until commit; CLUSTER takes a blocking AccessExclusiveLock so it waits behind the same SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE holder then completes; byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all sixteen (vacuum-conflict) and two (cluster-conflict) permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-23): cluster-conflict-partition promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationClusterConflictPartition (design 0118-0041) — the partitioned-table sibling of cluster-conflict byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all four permutations with NO engine change; ALTER TABLE OWNER TO does not recurse to partition children (tablecmds.c AT_ChangeOwner never recurses) so only the parent is owned by the role: upstream CLUSTER takes an AccessExclusiveLock on the named parent (waits behind a concurrent LOCK IN SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE MODE on the parent then completes on commit) and enumerates the leaves without locking them skipping every leaf the role does not own (cluster_is_permitted_for_relation false with the WARNING suppressed by client_min_messages=ERROR) so a leaf held in SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE is never touched and CLUSTER returns immediately; goopg clusterOp.Next is a no-op rewrite that locks only the named parent and never processes leaves so the captured output matches by both routes and the runner 300ms timing threshold renders the immediate-completion permutations without a waiting marker. M0118-0003 (2026-06-23): the FOR UPDATE/SHARE SKIP LOCKED row-lock family (skip-locked skip-locked-2 skip-locked-3 skip-locked-4) hardened from observability (runIsoSpec which skips a non-match) to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationSkipLocked/SkipLocked2/SkipLocked3/SkipLocked4 (design 0118-0042) — all four already match PG 18.3 byte-for-byte with no engine change; the switch enforces the M0118-0003-complete claim so a regression in the plain-lock / multixact-member-conflict / tuple-lock / updated-ctid-chain SKIP LOCKED skip paths surfaces as a red test instead of a silent skip. M0118-0008 (2026-06-23): vacuum-no-cleanup-lock promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationVacuumNoCleanupLock (design 0118-0045) — pg_class.relpages/reltuples now reflect what a non-aggressive VACUUM observes even while a cursor pins the only heap page: registered the vacuum_multixact_freeze_min_age GUC (the vacuumer setup SETs it) plus its postgresql.conf.sample line; new catalog.UpdateRelStats (the vac_update_relstats analog) publishes Pages/RowCount while merging into any existing Stats so a prior ANALYZE's pg_statistic survives; the virtual pg_class builder reads t.Stats (nil means 0|0 so untouched tables are unchanged); reltuples is published from vacuum.Analyze's fresh-snapshot visible-tuple count NOT the prune's surviving-line-pointer count so a recently-dead tuple (deleted+committed but not removable because the pin holder holds OldestXmin back) is excluded from reltuples exactly as PG counts HEAPTUPLE_LIVE not RECENTLY_DEAD — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-23): alter-table-2 promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationAlterTable2 (design 0118-0046) — the ALTER TABLE ADD FOREIGN KEY parser now accepts the NOT VALID trailer (in any order with [NOT] DEFERRABLE; convalidated='f' in pg_constraint) and ADD CONSTRAINT now takes a transaction-scoped ShareRowExclusiveLock on the altered table via acquireDDLLockTxn (AlterTableGetLockLevel → AT_AddConstraint) so a concurrent INSERT in RowExclusiveLock blocks until the ALTER transaction commits while a concurrent SELECT FOR UPDATE in RowShareLock proceeds — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all 48 permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-23): alter-table-1 promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationAlterTable1 (design 0118-0047) — the only new piece on top of alter-table-2's ADD FK NOT VALID is ALTER TABLE … VALIDATE CONSTRAINT name which now parses (new AlterTableValidateConstraint action; VALIDATE is an identifier-keyword) and takes only a transaction-scoped ShareUpdateExclusiveLock via acquireDDLLockTxn (AlterTableGetLockLevel → AT_ValidateConstraint the minimum lock) and flips the named FK's convalidated from 'f' to 't' (an unknown name raises 42704); ShareUpdateExclusive does not conflict with AccessShare reads RowShare FOR UPDATE or RowExclusive INSERT so VALIDATE never blocks the second session and the only wait in the spec is the INSERT behind the still-uncommitted ADD CONSTRAINT's ShareRowExclusiveLock exactly as in alter-table-2 — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all 170 permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-23): plpgsql-toast promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationPlpgsqlToast (design 0118-0054) — PL/pgSQL procedures with transaction control (COMMIT inside a DO block) where a second session's VACUUM runs (advisory-lock synchronized) between a variable's last assignment and its use across all six assignment code paths plus fetch-after-commit; two final pieces on top of 0118-0049..0053: a FOR-query loop now materializes its rows up front so the loop survives a DELETE/COMMIT in its body (PG holds the implicit cursor's snapshot across the commit) fixing assign6's three iterations and a SELECT … INTO inside a body now substitutes PL/pgSQL frame variables including record-field references like r.a before planning (substitutePlpgsqlFrameVarsInSQL) fixing fetch-after-commit; goopg stores text inline so the missing-chunk detoast correctness the spec guards is satisfied structurally — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all permutations; this is the last plpgsql-toast blocker so the spec is fully promoted. M0118-0008 (2026-06-24): detach-partition-concurrently-1 promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationDetachPartitionConcurrently1 (design 0118-0059) — ALTER TABLE … DETACH PARTITION … CONCURRENTLY is now two-phase keyed on a global mvcc partition-detach epoch (0118-0058 primitives wired): phase 1 NextPartitionDetachEpoch + MarkPartitionDetachPending keeps the child registered (relpartbound stays set so the s3i probe reads relpartbound IS NULL = f) while every snapshot taken afterwards captures the higher epoch and omits the child — READ COMMITTED sees it gone immediately while a REPEATABLE READ reader whose snapshot predates the detach still sees it until commit — then the detacher waits via the snapshot-based WaitForOlderSlotsToCommit (a RR session that has only PREPAREd a statement holds no lock yet is still waited for) and phase 2 unregisters the child and clears relpartbound so s3i flips f→t; both the SELECT planner expansion (collectAllPartitionLeaves) and INSERT routing (routeToPartitionDepth) filter the visible partition set through catalog.VisiblePartitionChildren by the snapshot epoch (sibling paths) and the cross-session plan cache is bypassed while any detach is pending (partitionDetachPending) so each statement re-plans against its own snapshot epoch — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all 13 permutations; detach-2 likely falls out of the same machinery while detach-3/4 still need persisted inhdetachpending/pg_partition_tree/FINALIZE/cancel-resume. M0118-0008 (2026-06-24): detach-partition-concurrently-2 promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationDetachPartitionConcurrently2 (design 0118-0060) — DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY makes the partition safe for a foreign key that references the partitioned table: the FK existence scan (assertParentExists -> allDescendants now filtered by ctx.Snap.PartitionDetachEpoch so a detach-pending leaf is invisible to a younger snapshot) makes a concurrent INSERT of a value living only in the detaching partition fail 23503 while a value in a still-attached partition succeeds; a referencing row committed before the detach whose key routes to the detaching partition makes the DETACH itself fail synchronously with removing partition X violates foreign key constraint <fkname>_<N> (RI_PartitionRemove_Check analog detachPartitionFKRefCheck run before MarkPartitionDetachPending so routeToPartition still resolves the child N=ordinal among the parent partitions); and the wait is now HYBRID — waitForRelationLockers on the parent and every partition leaf (READ COMMITTED sessions that touched the table hold a txn-scoped AccessShare to commit) plus WaitForPinnedSnapshotsToCommit (RR/SSI sessions holding a snapshot pinned before the detach via the new procSlot.pinnedSnap marker) so a READ COMMITTED session that only issued BEGIN holds neither and does NOT block the detacher — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all 5 permutations; detach-3/4 still need persisted inhdetachpending/pg_partition_tree/FINALIZE/cancel-resume. M0118-0008 (2026-06-24): detach-partition-concurrently-3 promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationDetachPartitionConcurrently3 (design 0118-0061) — a DETACH PARTITION CONCURRENTLY cancelled mid-wait now LEAVES the partition in the incomplete-detach state (the interrupt path no longer reverts MarkPartitionDetachPending) so it is omitted from every newer snapshot and from pg_partition_tree's parent (reported as a standalone NULL-parent root) and from TRUNCATE of the parent while DROP of the parent still cascades to it; ALTER on it raises 55000 cannot alter partition X with an incomplete detach and a second concurrent DETACH raises 55000 partition X already pending detach in partitioned table; DETACH FINALIZE completes it taking an AccessExclusiveLock on the partition via acquireRelLockMaybeTransient (a concurrent read/insert of the partition blocks until FINALIZE's transaction commits but a parent scan does not) and DROP of the pending child grabs an AccessExclusiveLock on the parent so a concurrent parent SELECT blocks; a partitioned-parent scan now also locks the parent relation (new SeqScan.LockParentOID) and an autocommit write takes a transient RowExclusiveLock symmetric with the read path so it blocks behind the partition's AccessExclusiveLock — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all 18 permutations; detach-4 still needs cancel-then-resume of the concurrent detach itself. M0118-0008 (2026-06-24): partition-drop-index-locking promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationPartitionDropIndexLocking (design 0118-0074) — a non-CONCURRENTLY DROP INDEX issued inside an explicit transaction now defers its catalog/relfile/WAL/pg_class-xmax removal to COMMIT (new BasicSession.pendingIndexDrops + ApplyPendingIndexDrops invoked before TxnMgr.Commit on both the executor execCommit and the server simple-query dispatch paths; EndExplicitTransaction discards the pending list on any ROLLBACK and CancelPendingIndexDropsToDepth drops entries recorded inside a rolled-back savepoint) so the dropped index stays in the shared catalog until commit and a third observing session's pg_locks JOIN pg_class still sees the index's pg_class row plus the dropper's AccessExclusiveLock (acquired top-down over the partition tree by the existing lockDropIndexTree from enablers 0118-0067..0073) — the transactional-DDL visibility piece that closes the last blocker; in autocommit the removal stays immediate (historical non-blocking behaviour); byte-identical to PG 18.3 across both permutations. M0118-0008 (2026-06-24): partition-concurrent-attach promoted to pass-required via runIsoSpecStrict in TestPort_IsolationPartitionConcurrentAttach (design 0118-0079) — closing the spec on top of enablers 0118-0075..0078; two final gaps: (Gap 1) PG ExecInsert opens every partition a tuple is routed into in RowExclusiveLock but goopg locked only the named INSERT target (tpart) and nothing along the routing path so an INSERT INTO tpart routing through the intermediate DEFAULT tpart_default never contended with a concurrent ATTACH's AccessExclusiveLock on that default — new lockRoutingPathPartitions walks the parent chain from the routed leaf up to (excluding) the named target and RowExclusive-locks each intermediate partition via acquireWriteLockTxn wired into insertOp.Next right after routing resolves the leaf so perm 1's INSERT waits behind the ATTACH then re-routes onto the now-visible tpart_2 raising 23514 and perm 3's INSERT holds the lock to commit so the ATTACH's lockDefaultPartitionForAttach acquire waits; RowExclusiveLock is self-compatible/DML-grade so concurrent partitioned INSERTs never block each other and single-level partitioned tables are a no-op; (Gap 2) the ATTACH default-content conflict scan checkDefaultPartitionDataConflict now refreshes its snapshot to TxnMgr.SnapshotFor(ctx.Tx) before scanning (mirrors the detach-4 post-wait RI re-validation 0118-0064) because the attaching statement's snapshot predates the lock wait and could not see the concurrent INSERT's just-committed rows so perm 3's ATTACH now finds them and raises 23P01 naming the leaf default tpart_default_default — byte-identical to PG 18.3 across all three permutations.
